keyVerseText: Sixteen years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned two and fifty years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.
rootMeaning: The name יְכׇלְיָה (Yᵉkolyâh) derives from the Hebrew root יָכֹל (yâkôl), meaning 'to be able' or 'to prevail,' combined with the divine element יָהּ (Yah), a shortened form of Jehovah. Thus, the literal meaning is 'Jehovah is able' or 'Jah will enable.' This etymology emphasizes God's sovereign power and enabling strength rather than mere human ability, highlighting divine empowerment as the foundation of the name.
usageInScripture: The word יְכׇלְיָה appears twice in Scripture, both times as a proper name referring to the same individual: the mother of King Uzziah (Azariah) and wife of King Amaziah of Judah. It is consistently translated as Jecholiah or Jecoliah, underscoring its identity as a personal name rather than a common noun. This consistency in usage reveals that the name serves to identify a historical figure whose name itself carries theological significance.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יְכׇלְיָה as 'Jehovah is able' reminds believers that God's power undergirds even the most ordinary aspects of history, such as the lineage of kings. This name points to the truth that God's enabling presence is foundational to the leadership and legacy of His people. It encourages faith in God's ability to empower His servants and fulfill His promises, reinforcing the trustworthiness of divine providence in the unfolding of redemptive history.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Kings 15:2, the verse states, 'Sixteen years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned two and fifty years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.' The mention of Jecholiah here not only identifies King Uzziah's mother but also subtly invokes the meaning of her name—'Jehovah is able'—suggesting that the king's reign is undergirded by God's enabling power. This enriches the verse by connecting the royal lineage with divine empowerment.
